inlineContent.text: A game is one type conforming to
, and the engine reads four things off it: the
values you declared as stored properties, which it finds by reflection and names after each property; a
block of exits and starting places; a
block of behavior; and an optional
block that teaches the parser new words.
builds one from an empty package.
The same value is both the declaration and the live reference:
reads its state inside a rule. That is the idea most of the rest follows from.
Each line the player types is parsed into a
and run through a fixed pipeline — world, location and item
rules, each-turn rules, and the timer tick. Any rule can
. Every change commits atomically at the end of the turn, which is also what
) — one small winnable game that exercises containers and a locked door, a fuse and a daemon, a roaming actor,
state, a content bundle, and two plugins. Most of the guides below link back to it.
After that the articles are a reference, not a sequence: read
when you want to know whether it works,
when you are ready to run a round, and
when the game refuses to start.
The package ships seven libraries beside the engine, each a separate product you import only if you want it:
(a time of day rather than a turn counter),
(asking, telling, showing, and what somebody has already been asked),

Each has its own documentation in this archive. They are not linked from here: a merged archive resolves symbol links only within a module, so a link across one would render as plain text rather than fail loudly. See
for how they splice in. The published archives, one per library:

abstract.text: A self-contained slice of a game’s world: its own rooms, items, and
state, plus the geography, rules, and verbs that go with them.
A round sends agents through a game, replays their evidence, and writes a report of confirmed and refuted findings. It is the author-facing workflow around the instruments in
Whether the location currently has light — its own (locations declared
start unlit; all others start lit) or a lit
item
shining here. Read and write are deliberately asymmetric: the getter
answers “is there light here”, the setter gives or removes the room’s
light and never touches any item’s lit state.

(enforced by the put-in action). The bootstrap warns when it is declared on
a non-container, where it has no effect.

intent a match produces. Data, not code — games can add rows through their
